baseline.firstProposedApproach: Initialize the handler stream reference from the accepted upgraded protocol stream, preserving the existing handler delegation.
baseline.rootCause: The handler retained a null stream reference even though the accepted protocol owned the active upgraded stream.

assisted.firstProposedApproach: Add interactive mode to the protocol contract, delegate it through FramedUpgradeProtocol to its stream, and update the stale handler caller while leaving the client-side control unchanged.
assisted.rootCause: The handler called a stale direct stream field after ownership moved behind UpgradeProtocol.

control.onlyIntentionalDifference: The treatment received the pre-registered concise TR-04 failure-aware capsule; control received no AEG experience.

retrieval.query: avoid repairing the wrong client-side surface when a public low-latency control broke after protocol stream ownership migration
retrieval.delivery: Only context, failed approach, recovery, and validated outcome were injected into treatment.

pathComparison.explanation: Control repaired handler initialization with one line. Treatment used the pre-registered canonical protocol-contract path. Neither changed RpcClientConnection or entered the known trap; both passed in one attempt.

interpretation.rationale: Treatment did not prevent a control failure and did not reduce attempts, commands, tests, or total non-cached tokens. Its lower duration was not sufficient under the frozen positive-result rule.

limitations: Control independently avoided the known client-side trap, so this pair does not show AEG preventing a control failure.
Treatment used one more command and 944 more total non-cached tokens; attempts and test executions were unchanged.
Treatment completed 7292 milliseconds faster, but wall time alone was not a pre-registered positive-result efficiency metric.
The patches are behaviorally correct but architecturally different; neither exactly matches the canonical patch hash because of implementation choice or method ordering.
One pre-registered pair cannot establish a generalized failed-path-prevention effect.
